newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Spotlight falls on police in Vietnam drugs probe.
newsitem.headline: Spotlight falls on police in Vietnam drugs probe.

text.p: Vietnam said on Monday it had arrested a senior drug squad policeman on suspicion of involvement in heroin trafficking, as government officials warned that narcotics abuse had become a nationwide scourge.

State media said Major Vu Huu Chu, a ranking official at the Ministry's Economic Police Department, had been arrested on evidence from the death-row confession of a convicted Laotian drugs trafficker.
The reports said Chu, deputy chief of the department's anti-drug abuse bureau, was the second senior policeman to be implicated.
Another officer, Vu Xuan Truong, was arrested just months ago after being named in evidence supplied by the Laotian, who won a stay of execution after breaking down in front of the firing squad.
Voice of Vietnam radio and several state dailies indicated that others were involved.

"This important drug case is being investigated by law enforcement agencies with a get-tough determination to deal with those members of the security apparatus who, due to their degeneration and deviation, have violated the law," the radio said.

International drug experts say Vietnam is awash with narcotics bound for Australia and the United States. The source of the drugs, mostly heroin, is the notorious Golden Triangle producing area on the borders of Thailand, Burma and Laos.
A United Nations drugs expert warned in October that heroin traffickers were targetting schoolchildren in a bid to create a market of juvenile dependency.
Hanoi, too, is aware of the problem.

Deputy Interior Minister Le The Tiem told a meeting on Saturday that police had uncovered 1,700 trafficking cases within the past two months, seized more than 200 kg (440 lb) of opium and heroin and were pressing charges against 840 people.

State media also reported that officials at a top-level government meeting last week had been told that Hanoi was stepping up its war against illegal narcotics and aimed to bring in tough new legislation to tackle the problem.
Participants were quoted as saying the drugs scourge had reached "every corner of life" in Vietnam, with 70 percent of the country's 180,000 addicts below 30 years in age.
The official Vietnam News Agency said new measures, including forced labour for addicts and the creation of a special drugs-busting authority, would be introduced.
"Timely and tough penalties must be given to all drug traffickers, dealers and abusers," VNA said.
